goal: Add optional type-checking flags (ALLOW_BOOL/INT/STRING/LIST) to ArgsManager so settings can be validated on startup and misuse of GetArg helpers raises clear errors instead of silent bugs.
No behavior change yet: the new flags are unused outside tests, but they unblock several follow-up PRs that apply the checks to real options.

result.summary: This PR adds ALLOW_BOOL, ALLOW_INT, ALLOW_STRING, and ALLOW_LIST flags to ArgsManager, enabling startup-time validation of setting values and internal consistency checks (raising logic_error) when GetArg-family functions are called with mismatched flags. It also updates GetArg/GetIntArg/GetBoolArg helper semantics to work cleanly with these new flags, avoiding known type-coercion footguns (e.g. -nowallet producing a wallet named "0"). The change is explicitly a no-op for existing behavior since the new flags are not yet applied to any real options; extensive new unit and fuzz tests exercise the new behavior.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core's ArgsManager currently does inconsistent, ad-hoc parsing of command-line and config settings (bools, ints, negation, multiple assignment) with well-documented bugs and confusing corner cases (see issues #17508, #30529), and callers frequently misuse IsArgSet/IsArgNegated. Developers adding or auditing settings, and users who hit confusing option parsing, both feel this; the PR is explicitly foundational infrastructure for a string of dependent PRs that apply stricter, well-defined semantics to real options.

open_concerns: maflcko: this large, all-at-once flag design bakes in a lot of interacting behavior that is hard to review as a whole, and would rather see the feature introduced and rolled out incrementally, one option at a time; ryanofsky disagrees this is necessary and explained tradeoffs but did not adopt the suggestion (2024-08 to 2024-09, unresolved, treated as agree-to-disagree by both).

hodlinator's exploration found several pre-existing rough edges (-noversion, -nodatadir, -conf directory-as-file bug) that this PR doesn't fully fix but doesn't worsen either; flagged as follow-up items, not blocking.

Whether to keep iterating with ALLOW_* bit flags versus migrating to the C++-type-based approach in the related PR #31260/#22978 is unresolved; author says the two approaches are largely orthogonal and this PR can merge independently.
resolved_concerns: ajtowns's approach objection to allowing flag combinations (ALLOW_INT|ALLOW_STRING etc.) was resolved when ryanofsky dropped that feature from the PR (commit dropping flag-combination support, 2024-08-23).
Numerous style/wording/refactor nits from l0rinc, hebasto, and hodlinator were implemented in follow-up pushes.

result.card: This long-running (since 2019) refactor adds ALLOW_BOOL/INT/STRING/LIST type-checking flags to Bitcoin Core's ArgsManager, enabling startup validation of settings and internal consistency checks between how options are registered and retrieved, with zero behavior change to existing options since the new flags are only exercised in tests. Its importance is almost entirely leverage: the author and reviewers cite it as the explicit foundation for four other open PRs (#17580, #17581, #17493, #17783) that use these flags to fix confusing, long-standing settings-parsing bugs (see issues #17508, #30529). Review history is unusually deep: an early blocking objection from ajtowns about flag-combination support was resolved by removing that feature outright, and more recent reviewers (l0rinc, hodlinator, laanwj) have given concept/approach ACKs, while maflcko's preference for a more incremental, per-option rollout remains an acknowledged but non-blocking disagreement. The PR is a draft but mergeable and CI-clean, with the author actively rebasing through 2026 despite no new substantive reviewer comments since October 2024, making it ready for a fresh review pass.
